chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from al-Ala' ibn Sabih and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Ali ibn Ri'ab and Abd Allah ibn Salih, all of them reporting it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The woman performing Tamattu', when she arrives in Mecca and then menstruates, stays in the period between her arrival and the Day of Tarwiyah. If she becomes pure, she circumambulates the House and performs Sa'ee between al-Safa and al-Marwa; and if she does not become pure until the Day of Tarwiyah, she performs Ghusl and stuffs herself (with cotton), then performs Sa'ee between al-Safa and al-Marwa.

Then she goes out to Mina. So when she fulfills the rituals and visits the House, she performs the Tawaf of her Umrah, then performs the Tawaf of the Hajj. Then she goes out and performs Sa'ee. So when she does that, she has been released from everything from which the Muhrim is released, except for the bed of her husband. So when she performs another seven circuits (Tawaf), the bed of her husband becomes permissible for her.

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ الْمُتَمَتِّعَةُ: The woman performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The one in Ihram (state of consecration)
key_terms.فِرَاشَ زَوْجِهَا: The bed of her husband (marital relations)

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual rulings for a menstruating woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the fiqh of Hayd (menstruation) during Hajj al-Tamattu', highlighting the scholarly consensus that Sa'ee can be performed in a state of minor or major impurity, though purification is preferred. It further clarifies the graduated release from Ihram restrictions, noting that while most prohibitions lift after the final Tawaf, marital intimacy remains forbidden until the completion of the seventh circuit, a nuance often discussed in Shia juristic commentaries.
